name: Archil

modes.label: Developer plan sandbox, fixed 2 vCPU / 4 GB ($0.27/h after 30 free min)
modes.note: Pricing page: 'Sandboxes are 2 vCPU · 4 GB RAM', 30 min/month included then $0.27/hr. The API accepts 1-32 vCPU / 0.25-64 GiB but only this size is priced publicly. On Developer ALL sandbox network egress is denied (and stays denied after upgrade until the policy is replaced). Persistent sandboxes are in preview and may be pre-empted. Prices are AWS us-east-1; 'other regions vary' (multiplier unpublished). Paused = no compute charge.

modes.label: Team plan sandbox, fixed 2 vCPU / 4 GB ($0.18/h after 1,000 included min)
modes.commit_note: Requires the $500/month Team plan (pure fee, buys 1 TB performance storage + 1,000 sandbox-min).
modes.note: 1,000 sandbox-min/month included, then $0.18/hr (33% below Developer). Network egress allowed on Team. Docs also say every 1 TB of active data yields 1,000 free sandbox-min; whether extra TB above the included 1 TB add minutes is unverified. Preview: may be pre-empted. us-east-1 prices; other regions vary.

evidence.quote: Network egress filters for sandboxes are limited to the Team plan and above. On the Developer plan, all network egress is denied.
By default, sandboxes have no restrictions on outbound internet access.

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: Included each month: 30 sandbox-min (= $0.135 at $0.27/h, encoded as included_usd) and 10 GB performance storage (then $0.30/GB-mo). Up to 5 file systems. No card required. Sandbox egress to the internet is DENIED on this plan.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: $500/month pure fee (not usage credit). Included: 1,000 sandbox-min (= $3.00 at $0.18/h, encoded as included_usd) and 1 TB performance storage (then $0.20/GB-mo, worth ~$200 at that rate). Unlimited file systems, orgs, BAA & DPA, sandbox egress enabled.

plans.name: Enterprise (BYOC / on-prem)
plans.note: Custom: unlimited storage with volume pricing (>50 TB discounts), committed spend, BYOC or on-prem, SSO & SCIM, 24/7 support, SLA, net-30 invoicing. Unpublished.

extras.price: Developer: 10 GB incl., then $0.30/GB-mo; Team: 1 TB incl., then $0.20/GB-mo; time-weighted average of cached/active data metered per minute
$0.025/GB-mo (file systems not syncing to a customer-owned bucket)
$0.05/GB when a file system is accessed out of region
1,000 free min/month per TB of active data; 100 ms minimum per call, 1 ms increments; rate beyond free unpublished

perf_source: ComputeSDK sandboxes benchmarks: cold_start_tti median 128.09 ms (run 2026-08-07), burst_tti median 237.39 ms at 100 concurrent (2026-09-25, p99 1.39 s). DAX never succeeded (0/14 runs), so dax_s null. No hpc CPU run.
caveats: Only one sandbox size is priced (2 vCPU / 4 GB) although the API accepts 1-32 vCPU and 0.25-64 GiB; prices for other sizes are unpublished, so larger workloads cannot be priced (linear scaling would be an assumption).
Persistent sandboxes are a preview (not flagged beta because they are the only sandbox product; treat as beta), may be pre-empted, and a host failure loses in-memory state.
Developer plan denies all sandbox network egress; real internet-using workloads need Team ($500/mo pure fee).
Billing granularity / minimum for sandbox time unpublished (the included allowance is expressed in minutes).

Pause is documented as stopping charges; storage cost of paused memory+disk snapshots and of the sandbox root disk is unpublished (snapshot_gib_month null). Data on an attached Archil disk bills as performance storage (see extras).

Performance storage conflict: pricing page says Developer $0.30/GB-mo after 10 GB and Team $0.20 after 1 TB; docs billing page still says a flat $0.20/GiB-mo and 'no egress fees'. Pricing page (newer, lists sandboxes) used.
The $0.05/GB egress applies to out-of-region file-system access, not to sandbox internet egress, whose price is unpublished (network.egress_gib null).
Prices are for AWS us-east-1; 'other regions vary' with no multiplier published. Sandboxes run in AWS regions only (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1).
Timeouts pause (not kill) since Sept 2026: hard TTL default/max 24 h but can be reset on a live sandbox; optional idle TTL off by default, so idle sandboxes keep billing until paused.
Docs: each 1 TB of active data grants 1,000 free sandbox-min; whether this stacks above the Team plan's included 1 TB is unverified.

Disk priced at Archil performance storage $0.20/GB-month (Team overage; Developer $0.30 after 10 GB): sandboxes are "colocated with your Archil disk data" and persistent data lives on the Archil disk. Team includes 1 TB account-wide, which the engine does not deduct (overstates disk for small fleets). Root-disk and paused memory-snapshot storage prices remain unpublished (snapshot_gib_month null). Source: archil.com/pricing, docs.archil.com/compute/sandboxes/introduction, 2026-09-28.

The Create Sandbox API default shape is 1 vCPU / 2 GiB (vcpu_count default 1, mem_size_mib default 2048; range 1-32 vCPU, 256-65536 MiB), while the pricing page only prices 'Sandboxes are 2 vCPU · 4 GB RAM'. Whether smaller/larger shapes bill the same $0.27/$0.18 per hour is unpublished.
Custom images: any public Linux OCI image (default ubuntu:26.04); private registry images are not supported yet.

Sept 2026 changelog: sandbox ports can be exposed publicly (any TCP over TLS with SNI) or privately via port tokens (HTTP/1.1 over HTTPS); firewall can drain in-flight requests before pause. No pricing change announced.

fleet.verification: No credit card needed to start; standard paid billing uses card via Stripe, Enterprise invoices.
fleet.notes: Persistent sandboxes are preview and may be preempted. Serverless command execution mentions hundreds in parallel and contacting Archil for thousands, but that is not a numeric persistent-sandbox account quota; defaults remain unknown.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A sandbox has a hard timeout and an optional idle timeout. Both pause the sandbox, preserving its disk, memory, and processes for `resume()`.
snapshot_auto.note: Triggered by hard TTL (default/max 24 h) or optional idle TTL (off by default); memory + running processes included. Since Sept 2026 (changelog). Traffic to an exposed port / port token auto-resumes a paused sandbox. Plain stop() is disk-only. Planned maintenance also pauses.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Checkpoints a running source sandbox and creates an isolated writable disk branch. Forks from running or paused sources resume from the source's CPU, memory, and disk state.
snapshot_on_demand.note: pause() snapshots CPU+memory+disk on demand; fork() of a running/paused/stopped sandbox creates new sandboxes from that state (memory included unless source stopped). No separate named-snapshot object for sandboxes; Archil disks additionally have branches/checkpoints.

harness_api.note: Full docs corpus (llms-full.txt) searched: only a generic processes/exec + PTY API; no Claude Code/Codex/etc. driver. AI guides use AI SDK with disk.exec as a bash tool (harness runs outside).

egress_allowlist.quote: The sandbox firewall operates on both the IP and transport layer, so you can filter both CIDR ranges and domains.
egress_allowlist.note: default allow/deny + allow/deny lists (IPv4/CIDR, exact or *. wildcard domains); live-updatable via updateNetwork. Developer (free) plan: all egress denied and policy cannot be changed; Team+ required.

egress_http_rules.quote: Allowed IPv4 addresses, CIDR ranges, exact domains, wildcard domains beginning with `*.`, or target objects with optional outbound HTTPS request transformations.
egress_http_rules.note: Rules match on host/IP only (rule schema is closed: target, transform.headers, forward_url). Header injection and forward_url (send matching requests to your own HTTPS endpoint, which could filter) exist, but no method/path/header matching.

ingress_rules.quote: For private access, leave the port unexposed and create a port token. Send the token in the `X-Archil-Token` header; requests without a valid token get `401`.
ingress_rules.note: Choose which ports to expose (public, any TCP over TLS+SNI, no auth) or keep private with expiring port tokens (HTTP/1.1 over HTTPS). Services private unless enable_service_ingress. No IP allowlists.

guest_firewall.note: Full Linux microVM, processes run as root (uid 0); not documented explicitly.

secret_proxy.quote: This means that secret credentials can live outside the sandbox, so untrusted workloads cannot access them directly. For example, you can add API keys to outgoing HTTP requests so your sandbox never sees them:
secret_proxy.note: Per-domain header transforms on the TLS-terminating egress proxy (Archil CA installed in sandbox). HTTP(S) only (ports 80/443); no DB/SSH/git-over-SSH coverage. Requires Team plan (egress).

volume_attach.quote: The Archil CLI comes prebaked into sandboxes, so you can attach an Archil disk to a sandbox by using the usual command to mount the disk:
volume_attach.note: Archil disks (S3-backed elastic POSIX FS) mounted from inside via `archil mount` with a mount token; each sandbox also has its own dedicated persistent disk.

volume_shared.quote: Archil supports sharing disks between multiple connected users simultaneously.
volume_shared.note: Read-write with delegations: exclusive mode (one machine), shared mode (read-only until `archil checkout <path>` write-lock), conditional mode (NFS-like, all unlocked files writable).

nested_virt.quote: Persistent sandboxes are built on full-featured Linux microVMs that are colocated with your Archil disk data for maximum security and performance.
nested_virt.note: Archil sandboxes are themselves Firecracker microVMs (a guest under AWS's hypervisor). No docs mention /dev/kvm passthrough or nested virtualization support inside a sandbox; microVM guests do not typically expose KVM to their own guests.

anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (Archil is a data-disk + persistent-sandbox/serverless-execution compute platform, not a browser/scraping product; no browser, computer_use, or stealth features exist in the docs).

captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no browser or CAPTCHA-related functionality anywhere in the docs; product is a general Linux sandbox/disk platform).

egress_ip_type.quote: our egress proxy must terminate TLS, so we install an "archil egress" proxy CA into every sandbox
egress_ip_type.note: Sandboxes run on AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1) and egress passes through Archil's own TLS-terminating egress proxy fleet; this is standard cloud/datacenter IP space, not residential/mobile. No specific IP range or static-IP guarantee is published.

ssh.note: No SSH access to persistent sandboxes is documented anywhere in the docs or API reference; interaction is via the processes/exec API and exposed TCP/HTTPS ports (public ports or private port tokens), not SSH. The only SSH content in the docs is an unrelated guide for self-hosting Archil inside your own Firecracker microVM.

live_resize.note: vCPU/RAM (1-32 vCPU, 0.25-64 GiB) are set only at sandbox creation. The full sandbox API surface (create/start/stop/pause/resume/fork/set-timeout/update-network/expose-port) has no update-resources/resize endpoint.

own_agent_api.quote: Run untrusted AI-generated code against context with tools based on serverless execution or traditional persistent sandboxes.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Archil provides generic compute/exec + disk storage for others to build agents on top of; it does not ship its own browser/computer-use/research task agent or an API to drive one.

mcp_server.quote: Add to your agent, [Mastra](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@archildata/mastra), or [LangChain](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@archildata/langchain). For more control, use our TypeScript SDK or Python SDK directly.
mcp_server.note: Docs list integrations (Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, LangChain) and TypeScript/Python/CLI SDKs, but no MCP server package or docs page exists anywhere in the full docs corpus.

lang_python.quote: Archil's serverless execution makes it simple to run untrusted code like bash, Python, and Node.js
lang_python.note: Also has a first-party Python SDK (docs.archil.com/sdks/python), and persistent sandboxes can boot any OCI image including python:3.13.

lang_node.quote: Archil's serverless execution makes it simple to run untrusted code like bash, Python, and Node.js
lang_node.note: Also has a first-party TypeScript/Node SDK (`disk` npm package) and persistent sandboxes can boot node:24-bookworm images.

max_session_h.note: Hard timeout (maxTtlSeconds) defaults to and maxes out at 86,400 seconds = 24 hours. It pauses (not kills) the sandbox and can be reset via setTimeout() before expiry to keep an active session going indefinitely across pause/resume cycles, but any single continuous run is capped at 24h before a pause is forced.

fork_running.quote: Checkpoints a running source sandbox and creates an isolated writable disk branch. Forks from running or paused sources resume from the source's CPU, memory, and disk state. ... A running source is resumed after its checkpoint; paused and stopped sources remain inactive.
fork_running.note: You CAN fork a running sandbox: docs confirm 'You can fork a running, paused, or stopped sandbox' and 'Forking a running sandbox pauses it while the snapshot is taken and resumes it once the fork is accepted' — the original keeps running (briefly paused for the snapshot only, same mechanism the card already credits under memory_snapshot_fork:true). Card's fork_running:false contradicts its own memory_snapshot_fork:true and snapshot_on_demand evidence; should be true.

desktop.quote: Persistent sandboxes are built on full-featured Linux microVMs that are colocated with your Archil disk data... Create long-running Linux VMs with persistent disks, interactive shells, services, and forks.
desktop.note: Archil is a headless Linux sandbox/VM + storage product (interactive shells, processes, ports) with no VNC/RDP/streamed GUI desktop anywhere in the docs. Outside the product's scope.

browser.quote: Create long-running Linux VMs with persistent disks, interactive shells, services, and forks.
browser.note: No managed/real browser offering in the docs; only mentions of 'browser' are the user's own web browser opening share URLs or the console file browser. Outside scope for a headless compute+storage product.

computer_use.note: Only a generic process/exec + PTY API is offered; no screenshot+click computer-use API exists. Consistent with no desktop/browser being offered at all.

agent_harnesses.note: Full docs corpus searched for Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode: none found preinstalled or offered as a template. Only generic exec/process API + AI-SDK-as-bash-tool guides (harness runs outside the sandbox). Matches existing harness_api:false evidence.

public_ipv4.quote: Exposed ports are public: they accept any TCP protocol over TLS with SNI, without authentication. ... For private access, leave the port unexposed and create a port token.
public_ipv4.note: Sandbox ports are reached via a TLS/SNI hostname or private port token, never a dedicated public IPv4 address per machine. No mention of a per-sandbox public IPv4 anywhere in the docs.

gpu.quote: Archil sandboxes run on x86-64 (`amd64`) and support between 1 and 32 vCPU cores and between 0.25 and 64 GiB of memory.
gpu.note: Sandbox spec is CPU/RAM only; no GPU instance type mentioned anywhere in pricing or docs (only unrelated mentions of faiss-gpu, a client library, in a tutorial).

windows.quote: Archil sandboxes run on x86-64 (`amd64`) and support between 1 and 32 vCPU cores and between 0.25 and 64 GiB of memory. Sandboxes run as the root...
windows.note: Sandboxes are Linux microVMs (custom images default to ubuntu); no Windows machine type is offered. Windows only appears in the docs as a client-OS caveat for the CLI/download tables, not as a sandbox OS.

macos.quote: Persistent sandboxes are built on full-featured Linux microVMs that are colocated with your Archil disk data...
macos.note: Compute (sandboxes) is Linux-only. Archil does ship a macOS *client* app (Archil for macOS, FSKit menu-bar app) for mounting disks locally, but that is not a macOS compute/sandbox machine, so the feature (macOS machines offered) is correctly false.

arm64.quote: Archil sandboxes run on x86-64 (`amd64`) and support between 1 and 32 vCPU cores and between 0.25 and 64 GiB of memory.
arm64.note: Sandbox compute is explicitly x86-64 only. arm64 binaries exist only for the client CLI/Lambda layer, not for sandbox machines.

self_host.quote: [contact us](mailto:support@archil.com) to learn more about our BYOC options for organizations with 100 TiB of data
self_host.note: Only a BYOC option (Archil-managed control plane deployed into the customer's own cloud account) is offered for large customers; there is no self-managed/open build customers can run entirely on their own infrastructure without Archil operating it.

open_source.quote: This page covers versioned, signed Linux releases only. It does not cover macOS, Windows, package-repository signing, Sigstore or Cosign attestations, or the unversioned `https://archil.com/install` script.
open_source.note: Only compiled client binaries/CLI and SDKs are distributed (no OSI-license source repo for the core sandbox/storage engine found in docs or a public GitHub org); the core Archil disk/sandbox engine is proprietary.

docker_inside.quote: Persistent sandboxes are built on full-featured Linux microVMs that are colocated with your Archil disk data for maximum security and performance. Create long-running Linux VMs with persistent disks, interactive shells, services, and forks.
docker_inside.note: Sandboxes are full Linux microVMs booting arbitrary public OCI images with root access (root=true) and a normal Linux kernel (the docs' Firecracker guide shows the guest kernel used is a standard compiled kernel, not a stripped-down one lacking overlayfs/cgroups). Running a nested `docker`/container runtime inside such a VM does not require nested virtualization (dockerd uses namespaces+cgroups, not KVM) and the docs describe mounting Archil disks into 'privileged' Docker containers assuming a full kernel underneath. No page explicitly confirms `dockerd` running inside an Archil persistent sandbox, so this is inferred from the full-VM/root architecture rather than a direct statement.

static_egress_ip.quote: our egress proxy must terminate TLS, so we install an "archil egress" proxy CA into every sandbox
static_egress_ip.note: All sandbox internet egress (when allowed, on Team+) is routed through Archil's own shared TLS-terminating egress proxy fleet, matched by domain/CIDR allow-deny rules. Docs never publish a fixed/dedicated outbound IP (or IP range) per sandbox or per account that a customer could allowlist on a third-party service; the egress feature set (firewall, allow/deny lists, header-injection secret proxy) is documented in detail with no mention of a static IP option, so it is treated as not offered rather than merely undocumented.

usage_api.quote: The Archil Control Plane API provides programmatic access to manage disks, mounts, and API keys. [Lists endpoints for Disks, Serverless Execution, Sandboxes, but no Usage or Metering endpoint]
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Billing page shows usage monitoring via console dashboard (Usage tab per disk, account-wide Billing page with real-time charts), but no REST API endpoint exists for programmatic usage retrieval per sandbox or by tag/project. Usage is only available dashboard for account.

locations_quote: Prices are for AWS us-east-1; 'other regions vary' with no multiplier published. Sandboxes run in AWS regions only (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1).
